assessment.reason: The plan accurately represents all seven transitions, distinct Close-summary and Back-introduction-h1 focus, the target already containing keyboard Back proof, and literal Tab versus preserved reverse/mixed procedure alternatives. It explicitly prevents one direction from being claimed as evidence of an unobserved direction.

The documentation requires exact sole-origin and GET/HEAD/OPTIONS enforcement before navigation and throughout requests, subrequests and redirects. It preserves unanswered scope and both checkpoints, prohibited actions, conditional blocked-analytics effects, fail-closed start and stop on breach/lost invariant.

The plan preserves fixture/historical provenance and distinguishes current target obligations, declarations, local consistency, proposed conventions and actual future observations. It does not call the already corrected Back instruction missing, or turn the fixture, count or blocked POST into a website defect/pass.

The correct relevant checker command has captured actual exit-zero output and its consistency-only disclaimer. Manual preservation/coverage review and thirteen substantive Gherkin cases supplement the limited checker. Spec-lint and run-check actual commands/results are retained separately from unexecuted browser acceptance.

The concrete proposal preserves the corrected target’s valid Close/Back traversal and Enter, both unanswered checkpoints, 24-step Back guard, introduction visibility/question-help absence and distinct focus. The exact help cycle and scope/evidence additions are justified. No application, contract/checker/policy or new runtime tooling change is proposed.

Actual frozen-source inspection identifies the remaining help-cycle/documentation omissions while rejecting a missing-Back diagnosis. A bounded one-document proposal, concrete source comparisons, substantive challenge/adjudication and captured local check support the selected planning outcome.

comparison.reason: Separate evaluators and verifier retained task/coverage observations. One observation on related known tasks and visible conditions does not establish a comparative winner; live deployment comparability is unverified for UX.

limitations: One observation on a related known task, not a general benefit benchmark.
